lots.working: Keep: lowest same-pattern SOLD A$214 / 1.22 = 175.4, round down to $175 (all-in $213.50). Flip: likely local resale about A$285 (the Aug 2026 82-piece result), less 15% selling fee (A$43) and $0 postage (pickup-only sale for a service this size) = A$242; / 2.44 = 99.2, round down to $95 (all-in $115.90).
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read clearly in the photos and there are 4 SOLD results, which would normally mean High. But the prices come from US sales, three are 5 to 13 years old, and I could only read them from the search results page because the item pages are bot-challenged, so condition was not checked.

Its snippet-only eBay asking prices (204025143438 US$279.30, ebay.de 388615759326, 176797786096) were not re-opened (eBay closed to us) and are not used. lots.key_photo_findings: Back-stamp read in photo 4: 'Bone China / mikasa / NARUMI - JAPAN / HARROW / 123'. Wide gold-encrusted scrolling band on ivory, fine inner gold line. Photo 1 shows about 12 dinner plates, 12 salad plates, 12 side plates, around 24 saucers, 12 cups (one stacked set on the left), about 12 small bowls, a rimmed serving bowl and an oval platter. Gilding looks bright in the close-ups, with no obvious rubbing, but only a few pieces are shown up close.
lots.condition: Looks clean and bright where visible. Gold wear, chips and crazing can't be checked across the whole set from 4 photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the piece count, and whether there is any gold wear, chips or cracks on the plates and cup rims?
